key_insight: LDNet is extended to handle variable initial conditions by inferring the initial latent state from early observations, enabling resolution-independent surrogate prediction for time-dependent PDEs.
engineering_relevance: This makes fast many-query simulation feasible for solid mechanics and other PDE-driven engineering systems without retraining for each new starting state or mesh.
method: Encode early-time observations into a task-specific latent initial state.
Evolve the latent state with Neural ODE dynamics.
Decode high-resolution fields with a coordinate-based decoder; compare auto-decoding vs meta-learning for latent initialization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports successful evaluation across advection-diffusion, fluid dynamics, and solid mechanics, with meta-learning accelerating latent-state inference and improving optimization conditioning.
watch_item: Performance depends on having sufficiently informative early-time observations, and latent-state inference may be sensitive to observation quality and coverage.
paper_title: Learning PDE solution operators with variable initial conditions via Latent Dynamics Networks
